title: Cable Lateral Raise
summary: A one-arm lateral raise from a low cable: side delts 1. The cable loads the bottom of the range that a dumbbell leaves light.

equipment_needs.text: Needs: cable station with an adjustable pulley.

muscles.why: The side delt lifts the arm out to the side. A dumbbell's resistance is near zero with the arm at your side; a cable pulling from across the body keeps it loaded from the start.
The traps rotate the shoulder blade upward as the arm rises; minor (0.3).

setup.text: Set the pulley at its lowest point and stand side-on, working arm away from the stack.
Hold the handle across the front of your body; hold the machine with the other hand.
Step out until the weight lifts slightly off the stack at the start.

form_cues.cue: Raise the arm out to the side
form_cues.why: Starting across the body means the side delt is loaded from the first degrees.

form_cues.cue: Keep a slight bend in the elbow
form_cues.why: Shoulder height is the end of the side delt's main range.
Controlling the return keeps the load on in the stretch.
A shrug moves the work to the upper traps.

bias_tweaks.change: Cable behind your body instead of in front
bias_tweaks.effect: Changes where in the range the cable pulls hardest; many lifters find one path smoother.
Starts the arm further across the body for a longer loaded range.

bias_tweaks.change: Lower in 2-3 seconds and pause briefly in the stretch
bias_tweaks.effect: Keeps tension on in the lengthened position and removes bounce, so each rep starts honestly.
bias_tweaks.caveat: Rep speeds from 0.5 to 8 s gave similar growth; this is a control tool, not a growth trick.

mistakes.text: Shrugging the trap up as the hand rises.
mistakes.fix: Hold on to the machine and keep the torso still.

mistakes.text: Bending the elbow more as the set gets hard.
mistakes.fix: Fix a slight bend and keep it.

mistakes.text: Standing too close, so the cable goes slack at the bottom.
mistakes.fix: Step out until there is tension at the start.

misconceptions.myth: Cables are better than dumbbells for side delts.
misconceptions.reality: The cable spreads tension more evenly; whether that grows the delts more has not been compared in a study the app cites.
Light and heavy loads gave similar growth when sets were taken close to failure. Heavy loads build more strength.

lower_risk.text: The app adds no ramp-up sets here. If the muscle is not warm from earlier work, make the first set a little lighter.

Add load in small steps. The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 10% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first, up to 2 past the top of the range. Default steps for this equipment are 2.5 kg or 5 lb; your gym profile can replace them.
Aim for about 2 reps in reserve in the 10-15 rep range. Low-risk to push close to failure; stop when the torso starts to lean to finish reps.
Pick a variation, range and setup you can train pain-free.

alternatives.why: Both arms at once with dumbbells; less load at the bottom.
Seated dumbbell raise; harder to cheat.
Raising in a Y adds more trap work.

notes: Side-delt variation choices are biomechanics or modeled.
Ratings and display bands are the library model (main >= 0.75, helper 0.4 to < 0.75, minor 0.25 to < 0.4, not counted < 0.25).
Technique and load management only. This page makes no medical or injury claims.
